title: feat(routing): Add dual-scheme BIN routing for Provider X with temporary fallback
author: devon.chen
content:
PR Summary:
Implements BIN routing logic in `PaymentRouter.ts` to direct French (CB) and German (Girocard) issued cards to the newly added `ProviderXGatewayAdapter`. Includes synchronous 3DS2 challenge dispatch.

Review Comments:
- elena.rostova (2024-07-10 17:05): LGTM on the BIN routing table. Quick question: did we consider Provider Z for this routing tier? Their transaction pricing was notably lower.
- devon.chen (2024-07-10 17:15): Yes, we tested Provider Z in staging sandbox last month. Provider Z failed our 3DS2 test suite: they do not support synchronous merchant challenge redirection, and their webhook callback arrived 4 minutes after the cardholder completed authentication on mobile. Users would be staring at a loading spinner. That disqualifies Provider Z for European card flows.
- marcus.vance (2024-07-10 18:00): Approved. We have to tolerate Provider X's legacy XML payload formatting for now. Remember this adapter is temporary for Q3/Q4 2024.

title: fix(reconciliation): Add retry buffer for Provider X missing settlement webhooks
author: sarah.k
content:
PR Summary:
Adds an in-memory Redis buffer and exponential backoff retry worker (`SettlementRetryQueue`) specifically for Provider X batch webhook ingest.

Review Comments:
- tariq.ahmed (2025-02-14 13:20): Is this retry logic needed for all our payment providers or just Provider X?
- sarah.k (2025-02-14 13:35): Only Provider X. Our domestic US gateways deliver webhooks within 500ms at 99.99% reliability. Provider X drops connection bursts during European market close (around 17:00 CET) without queuing them on their end. Without this 48-hour retry buffer, our automated ledger balance fails every Friday.
- tariq.ahmed (2025-02-14 14:02): Pretty frustrating considering Provider X contractual SLA promised high availability. Approving as a necessary safeguard for operations.

title: refactor(gateway-interface): Decouple payment-orchestrator from ISO-8583 message formatter
author: devon.chen
content:
PR Summary:
Isolates the legacy ISO-8583 socket formatting logic into an optional standalone plugin module (`legacy-iso-bridge`), allowing the core orchestration engine to run purely on JSON/gRPC contracts.

Review Comments:
- marcus.vance (2026-01-22 15:30): This is great work. With this separation, is anything outside of Provider X and the Apex Retail legacy socket server still touching ISO-8583 code?
- devon.chen (2026-01-22 15:42): Nothing else. Once Apex Retail finishes their REST API v2 migration (ticket PAY-3310), this legacy module will literally only be kept alive because Provider X's EU gateway requires XML-wrapped ISO 8583 bitmaps. If we switch to a modern European provider, we can delete this entire module and drop 12,000 lines of legacy code.
